When a merge conflict was resolved, the user has to press the 'continue' button to finish the merge again. 

When this is occurring, the dialog remains open and nothing seems to be happening. This is not a good user experience.

First thing we need to check: why does this dialog remain open for so long after user pressed 'continue'. Is this really required?

Secondly, how can we improve it so the user has a better feedback that processes are running. for instance, we can activate the animation on the worktree selector button? But also, if the dialog needs to remain open, we should add an animation like a spinner there as well, with some text to let the user know what is happening.

entries.content: The visible symptom is confirmed: pressing Continue sets the shared service to “busy,” disables controls, and leaves the dialog otherwise unchanged until the entire desktop operation returns. I’m now separating the necessary Git work from slower post-merge finalization to identify what actually holds it open.

design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:25:The desktop owns the active merge conflict session for one paused Git rebase or worktree integration. The renderer keeps a snapshot of that session to display the conflict dialog.
design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:29:While the reload is pending, the renderer still exposes the ended session and leaves the conflict dialog interactive. Continuing during that interval reaches the desktop after its session has already been cleared and produces `No active merge conflict session`.
design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:33:Close the renderer session immediately when the desktop reports that it ended. Capture the accumulated conflicted paths first, clear the session snapshot and affected-path tracking, and let the conflict dialog close without waiting for project data to reload.
design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:35:After closing the session, reload the captured paths when project storage is available. `ProjectLoading.reloadConflictPaths` must retain its current filtering, so only affected card Markdown is reloaded and ordinary source files require no renderer work. Report reload failures through the existing error path, but do not restore an ended session or reopen the conflict dialog.
design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:37:Use one idempotent session-closing path for desktop null events, successful Continue, successful Cancel, and verification that finds no active desktop session. This path must consume the captured paths once so concurrent notifications do not cause duplicate reloads. Preserve the existing integration activity and branch-cleanup processing after a successful Continue.
design/feature_descriptions\B_375_error_no_active_merge_conflict_session.md:39:Add focused service tests for immediate session closure, asynchronous card reload, ignored source paths, reload failure, and duplicate end notifications. entries.content:
## Findings

- Continue leaves the dialog open because `busy` only disables its controls; no progress indicator or text changes are rendered. [merge_conflict_dialog.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/merge_conflict_dialog.tsx:61)
- The operation performs more than continuing Git. It commits pending writes, completes the rebase/squash, synchronizes and refreshes worktrees, optionally deletes the branch, and records activity history. [local_bridge_dispatch.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js:456)
- The desktop deliberately retains the conflict session until cleanup and history recording succeed, allowing Continue to retry failed finalization safely. [local_bridge_dispatch.js](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/shell/local_bridge_dispatch.js:484)
- The worktree-selector animation stops when the initial integration returns a conflict, so it does not cover the later Continue operation. [worktree_service.ts](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/project/worktree_service.ts:403)
- There is no timing instrumentation, so the exact slow sub-operation cannot currently be identified.

## Proposed solution

Keep the dialog open because it remains the retry surface, but show a spinner and “Finishing integration and updating project…” while Continue is running. Change the button label to “Finishing…” and retain disabled controls.

Do not rely on the worktree-selector animation as the primary feedback because the selector may not be visible. If desired, extend the service-owned operation state so the selector also reflects conflict finalization.

Add duration logging around Git completion, worktree refresh, branch cleanup, and activity recording. Optimize only the phase shown to be slow.
